content:
Dev Patel: Dropping the draft macro/snippet refresh here for review 🙏
https://drive.google.com/…/support-macros-and-snippets-refresh

Main asks:
1) tone (esp enterprise / exec escalations)
2) required diagnostics (what do we *always* ask for before paging)
3) anything that feels risky/customer-unsafe

Priya Shah: skimming now. big +1 on consolidating these — half the time we’re rewriting the same 5 questions

Owen Phillips: love it. first pass: can we standardize on “request_id” vs “request IDs” vs “x-request-id”? I’d like the macro to explicitly say “paste 3–5 request IDs from failures”

Wei Chen: +1. also in Hosted macros, tone is good but a couple lines feel a little too internal.
Example: “our gateway is flapping” → I’d change to “we’re seeing intermittent connection issues”

Kira Thompson: For Private macros, the “send installer logs” section needs a safety line: “please redact secrets/tokens; don’t share customer data payloads.”
Also specify *which* logs: installer output + cluster events + version

Rafael Mendes: from on-call side: we need a hard requirement in the “Escalate to Eng” macro:
- region
- model + version (or ‘latest’)
- time window (with timezone)
- request IDs
- whether streaming + transport (http/2?)
Without those we’re burning cycles.

Dev Patel: makes sense. I can add a “Required for escalation” block at top of each macro and keep the rest optional.

Rachel Kim: Tone: I like the “thank you / we’re on it” framing, but let’s avoid promising cadence unless we’re sure we can meet it.
Some macros say “we’ll update every 30 minutes” — that should probably reference the SLA table instead (“we’ll provide updates per your support tier; next update by <time>”).

Priya Shah: Agree. Maybe add placeholders:
- Next update by: ___
- Current status: Investigating / Identified / Mitigating / Monitoring
So we don’t hardcode intervals.

Dylan Brooks: On required diagnostics: can we align with the intake checklist fields we’re making mandatory in Jira? (region, model, SDK version, request IDs, customer tier)
If the macro asks for the same fields it’ll reduce churn.

Dev Patel: yep. I’m trying to mirror the intake checklist + the Jira required fields.

Owen Phillips: also: add an “If you’re using our SDK, please share version + retry settings” line.
We keep getting “I upgraded” but no version number.

Wei Chen: For 429/rate limit macro, can we include “please paste the full response headers containing x-ratelimit-*” and clarify they should *not* paste API keys.

Dev Patel: good call. I’ll add:
- paste headers only
- don’t paste Authorization / api key

Rafael Mendes: Another on-call ask: “if you can, reproduce with curl and share the sanitized command (no keys)”. Helps us isolate SDK vs gateway.

Kira Thompson: careful for Private customers — curl reproduction may not be feasible due to VPC / mTLS. Maybe make it conditional: “if possible” + “or share a minimal request description (endpoint, payload size, streaming on/off)”.

Priya Shah: There’s a “please send logs” macro that currently asks for “gateway logs” — customers can’t get those. Maybe rename to “client-side logs” and “console screenshot of error + request IDs”.

Dev Patel: yep, that’s a bug. Will fix wording.

Elliot Price: Docs consistency: please link macros to the new Known Issues index whenever there’s a published workaround.
E.g. streaming disconnect macro should link to the streaming timeout/reconnect KB article. If it’s not published yet, mark “(internal draft)” and remove before publish.

Wei Chen: +1, and if we link KB, let’s keep language consistent (“workaround” vs “fix”).

Owen Phillips: Tone nit: replace “we need you to” with “could you please” in a couple spots. Some macros read a little sharp.

Dev Patel: ack. I’ll do a tone pass to soften imperative language.

Rachel Kim: For credits macro: we should avoid any “we will issue credits” language. Make it:
- we’ll review per contract
- we’ll confirm eligibility after impact is understood
- approvals needed (CS lead / exec escalation if large)

Dev Patel: yep. I’ll update credits macro to be “request received + next steps” only.

Rafael Mendes: For the “Page SRE” macro, add a line: “include dashboards links if you have them” but don’t block escalation on it.
Support rarely has the right dashboard handy.

Dylan Brooks: maybe include the canonical “Support-safe quick view” once ENG-4823 lands. For now could be “optional: console latency chart screenshot”.

Priya Shah: In the streaming macro, can we explicitly ask:
- are you behind a proxy/load balancer?
- any corporate egress?
We see a ton of resets from intermediaries.

Wei Chen: And mention recommended client timeout defaults (but keep it generic): “set a read timeout >= N seconds for long generations.”

Dev Patel: Noted. I’ll align with the SDK troubleshooting language so we don’t contradict docs.

Kira Thompson: Private upgrade macro: include “diagnostics bundle” wording but label it “if available” until the installer PR ships.

Dev Patel: good catch — will add “if your version supports it” and otherwise list manual artifacts.

Elliot Price: Process: when you update the macros doc, can you also add a small “How to use” section (when to use macro vs when to write custom) + where these live (Zendesk/Jira templates)?

Dev Patel: yep. I’ll add a preamble + mapping of macro → scenario + link to Confluence playbook.

Owen Phillips: last ask: add a “when to escalate” footer to each macro. Even a single sentence like “If impact is multi-customer / region-wide, we will open a bridge + involve on-call.”

Dev Patel: 👍 will do. I’ll incorporate changes today and re-share v2 for final :eyes: tomorrow.

Priya Shah: :thumbsup: happy to do final tone pass once you’ve revised

Rafael Mendes: :+1: thanks — this will save on-call a lot of back-and-forth

Rachel Kim: :thumbsup: ping me when credits + enterprise comms macros are updated, I’ll sanity check

Dev Patel: will do
